0.label: four_ribbed_arcs
0.description: Four long curved forms, smooth above and banded with rings and zigzags toward their ends, laid side by side against the right edge of the central disc beneath a crocodile.
0.iconography: They read most like carved elephant tusks or horns — ivory as royal wealth, horns as trumpets or medicine containers. Placed as a bracket to the disc, they may also be the crocodile's ribbed tail. Four of them: a small count worth noting.

1.label: hatched_creature_right_border
1.description: In the right border, a creature with a large round eye and a beaked head over a cross-hatched body, with a leaf spray to its left and a second hatched form below.
1.iconography: Perhaps a bird (hornbill or fowl) or a chameleon seen side-on; with the leaves, part of the tray's inventory of bush life.

2.label: crowned_face_oju_opon
2.description: At the head of the tray, a projecting face with lidded eyes, straight nose and radiating whiskers, under a bar of three studs and a crown of three large bosses.
2.iconography: The ojú ọpọ́n face of Ẹ̀ṣù, here crowned: the messenger given a king's headdress, which sets a royal tone for the whole border.

3.label: standing_man_with_staff
3.description: In the left border, a naked male figure standing frontally with a chevron-patterned torso band, holding an upright staff or spear at his side.
3.iconography: A man of standing, or a guard, with a staff of office or a spear; the counterpart to the load-bearer below him (#6).

4.label: inverted_squatting_figure
4.description: In the upper right border, a figure carved head-down with legs splayed upward and hands at the knees, beside small leaves, oriented toward the centre of the tray.
4.iconography: An inverted or tumbling figure; on trays, figures are often turned to face the working field, but head-down figures can also mark a fall or a birth.

5.label: reclining_figure_with_long_beaked_bird
5.description: On the lower border, a figure lying on its back with a patterned torso, arm raised, and at its feet a bird with a long beak.
5.iconography: Reclining figures recur around this border; the bird may be a hornbill or a fowl for sacrifice. Rest, sickness or death, with the offering beside it.

6.label: figure_supporting_load_on_head
6.description: In the left border, a standing figure with both arms raised to steady a load or bowl on its head.
6.iconography: A carrier or caryatid: the porter, or a devotee bringing an offering, a common figure on tray rims and veranda posts alike.

7.label: splayed_figure_with_goggle_eyes
7.description: In the lower-right corner, a figure with large round eyes and a hatched body lying with limbs splayed, beside a hatched cone-shaped form.
7.iconography: Possibly a frog or tortoise-like creature rather than a person; the cone may be a fish or a bundle. Low certainty.

8.label: crocodile_over_small_animal
8.description: Right of the head face, a crocodile with a long toothed snout and scaled back rears upward, with a small quadruped head beneath it.
8.iconography: The crocodile, power of the river and of dangerous authority, seizing or standing over a lesser animal. It sits directly above the four ribbed arcs (#0), which may be its tail.

9.label: serpent_coiled_round_animal
9.description: In the arc left of the disc, a long scaled snake coiling in loops around a smaller animal with a pointed head.
9.iconography: A python taking its prey, or a serpent binding a creature: the coil as capture and containment, close to the collection's ouroboros theme but not tail-biting.

10.label: monkey_holding_ring
10.description: In the upper-left arc, a figure with a round-eyed, monkey-like head and a zigzag-banded body, holding a looped ring or coil against its side.
10.iconography: The monkey, trickster and imitator, beside a ring; compare the monkey near the leaders on the Ado-Ekiti door (EBA-Div_00303 #32).

11.label: columns_of_leaves
11.description: Beside the tab at the foot, two columns of stacked veined leaves separated by a raised rib.
11.iconography: Medicinal leaves (ewé), the domain of Ọ̀sanyìn: the herbal remedies that often follow an Ifá prescription.

12.label: two_reclining_figures_top_right
12.description: In the top-right border, two figures lying head to foot, one with a patterned torso, the other raising an arm that holds a short object.
12.iconography: Reclining figures, one perhaps armed or carrying a tool; scenes of rest, sickness or struggle that recur around this border.

13.label: reclining_figure_holding_cord
13.description: On the lower-left border, a bearded figure lying on its back with legs drawn up, holding a long looped cord that arches over its body.
13.iconography: A figure bound or holding a rope; cords on trays can mean binding, captivity, or the tether of an animal to be sacrificed.

panel.title: Rectangular Ifá tray: crowned face, crocodile, tusks and a crowded world
panel.object_type: opon Ifá, rectangular with a central disc
panel.summary: A wide tray with three working fields (a disc between two rectangles) and a border packed with figures, animals and objects. A crowned, whiskered face projects at the top; a crocodile stands beside it above four ribbed tusk-like arcs; the rest of the border holds weapons, a drum, a studded board, leaves, snakes, monkeys and people.

register_readings.reading: Top border: the crowned face at the centre; to its right a crocodile over a small animal and two reclining figures. To its left (unboxed) a cutlass, a drum, a studded board and a reclining figure.

Sides and arcs: a standing man with a staff and a load-bearer on the left border; a monkey with a ring and a serpent coiled round an animal in the left arc; the four ribbed arcs against the disc; an inverted figure and a hatched creature on the right border.
Foot: a figure holding a looped cord, columns of leaves by the tab, a reclining figure with a long-beaked bird, and a splayed creature in the corner.

panel.composition: Three fields on one horizontal axis, a face and tab on the vertical axis, and a border that fills every gap. Left and right halves answer each other loosely rather than mirror.
panel.narrative: The border reads like an inventory of a town's life around the place where Ifá speaks: weapons and a drum (war and festival), a game board, medicinal leaves (ewé, the domain of Ọ̀sanyìn), people carrying and reclining, and the dangerous animals — crocodile, snake — that sacrifice keeps at bay. The crowned face and the tusks give the whole a royal note.
panel.hypotheses: Some support for carving as an archive of social life, not of rulers. Small counted groups (four arcs, rows of leaves) are possible but untested counts.
cross_panel_links: Snake coiling round a figure and monkeys: the Ado-Ekiti door's monkey (EBA-Div_00303 #32).
Three-field layout is unique in the collection.
uncertainties: The left field and the unboxed top-left objects are read from the photograph.
The arcs could be a tail, horns or tusks; the studded board could be a bed or a basket.
